messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: inference-pool-usw-2: pod churn + node NotReady spike (7 nodes) detected; avg 95th latency up 2.3x; errors: container_restart/oom/kubelet_restart. PagerDuty: primary oncall paged.
Sam (oncall): seeing it, joining. I’m going to mute noisy alerts and gather quick scope.
Sam (oncall): @InfraBot can you dump nodes in that pool and recent kubelet events?
InfraBot: requested: /api/internal/k8s/nodes?label=inference-pool=usw-2 -> returning 12 nodes, 7 NotReady. cmd: `kubectl get nodes -l inference-pool=usw-2 -o wide`
InfraBot: ```
NAME                          STATUS     ROLES    AGE    VERSION
ip-10-0-2-11.usw2.internal    NotReady   <none>   32d    v1.24.8
ip-10-0-3-14.usw2.internal    NotReady   <none>   14d    v1.24.8
ip-10-0-4-21.usw2.internal    NotReady   <none>   6h     v1.24.8
... (4 more NotReady)
```
Sam (oncall): ok, repeating kubelet restarts in kernel logs. grabbing pod restarts for inference runtime.
Sam (oncall): `kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=redwood-runtime -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{" "}{.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount}{"\n"}{end}'` -> lots of 5-30 restarts on the same pods.
Maya: logs show CUDA driver messages right before crash on a subset: `E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:... failed to allocate memory` then container OOM killed.
Liam: seems like a cascade: a kernel upgrade last week + a newer driver in image? any recent infra change?
Anika: no infra deploys in last 48h. There was an image push to runtime-canary 3h ago (small GC tweak). Not to production, but nodes with canary label are mixed in same pool accidentally.
Sam (oncall): that could explain memory pressure if canary uses different allocator. For mitigation: 1) isolate affected nodes via cordon, 2) create emergency scale (spin spare nodes) 3) move traffic to fallback model variant (smaller memory), 4) open customer-impact note.
Raj - support: customers A and B reported increased latency/errors on hosted API, roughly from 08:12 UTC. Incidents page updated.
Sam (oncall): cordoning now: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-4-21.usw2.internal` -> done for 4 nodes (manually cordoned the badly flapping ones).
Maya: starting scaling: increasing node pool target by +6 instances and triggering immediate bootstrap. ETA for new nodes ~3m.
Liam: routing change: can we temporarily steer traffic to model-small variant? It's compatible fallback.
Sam (oncall): updating router policy to prefer small-model variant for requests with latency < 200ms requirement. Patching route config.
Sam (oncall): `PATCH /v1/routes/inference-global` -> applied. Traffic shift ~80% away from the flapping pool within 45s.
InfraBot: new nodes joining: 4/6 ready after kubelet boot; kube-proxy stable.
Maya: monitoring pod restart counts. Creating a daemonset that sets `oom_kill_disable=false`? wait no, that's unsafe. We'll instead increase eviction threshold temporarily on affected nodes via kubelet flags -> patching via MachineConfig is slow. Alternative: mark nodes unschedulable and rely on new nodes.
Anika: I’m spinning a targeted emergency job to evict heavy-cache pods (large KV cache) off the flapping nodes to relieve memory.
Sam (oncall): good. Also enable node-level memory pressure alerts at lower thresholds so we don't chase full OOMs.
Liam: logs (excerpt) from runtime pod before crash: ```
[2026-03-15T08:10:11Z] runtime: cudaDriverMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T08:10:12Z] runtime: fallback to cpu path
[2026-03-15T08:10:13Z] oom_killer invoked: Killed process 1123 (redwood-runtime) total-vm:45G
```
Maya: looks like some nodes triggered oom_killer and kubelet then restarted the container; repeated restarts triggered eviction loops.
Sam (oncall): customer impact: degraded throughput and increased error rate in us-west region; support ticket created and customers notified. No data plane leak reported.
Raj - support: customers acknowledged the temporary mitigation plan. Support will coordinate updates.
Anika: can we patch runtime image to drop a memory-hungry cache keyed by default for a few minutes? If we can switch canary to production quickly, that'll help.
Liam: timeline: can push image with cache disable in ~20m, but we already have traffic moved. prioritize bringing pool back healthy.
Sam (oncall): escalation: @Maya take primary, I will go to sleep after handoff in 15m. Documenting runbook steps in incident doc.
Maya: taking over. Current action items: 1) finish scale-up and wait for nodes ready 2) drain cordoned nodes once stable 3) monitor latency/error burn-down 4) consider rollback of canary image if we confirm it's root cause.
Maya: creating incident ticket INC-2026-212 in tracker and linking logs/graphs.
InfraBot: monitoring: node flaps decreasing after scale and cordons; 3 nodes still NotReady (kubelet restart cycles).
Anika: eviction job succeeded on 6 pods; memory pressure reduced on 5 nodes. Pod restarts dropped to <=2 in most hosts.
Maya: rolling drain plan for the 3 remaining bad nodes: `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data <node>` sequentially with 2m wait. Starting now.
Sam (oncall): :thumbsup: leaving page with summary in pager duty and handoff note: "Mitigations applied: cordon bad nodes, scale +6, route shift to small-model, eviction of heavy caches. Next: drain remaining nodes and consider image rollback."
Raj - support: customers updated at 08:40 UTC. Waiting on final confirmation before closing customer impact message.
Maya: last node drained and rebooted. kubelet stable on all nodes. Monitoring for 30m window for reoccurrence.
Maya: CPU/GPU mem profiles look normal now, 95p latency back to baseline. Marking incident as mitigated; still creating postmortem.
Sam (oncall): thanks team. Postmortem owners: Maya + Anika. Action items: better pool label hygiene (no mixing canary), autoscaler warm spare buffer, kubelet restart alerting, runtime memory-usage regression test in CI.
incident-bot: Incident mitigated (status: partial-resolved) — incident channel: #incidents/3957654321, incident doc: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-212
Maya: assigning follow-ups, will post postmortem draft tomorrow. :memo:
